question: Should OpenClaw adopt default-on user-specific memory isolation in core memory-core, and if so what exact config/default/upgrade contract should it expose?
rationale: This PR changes a privacy and session-state boundary, adds config/default semantics, and conflicts with current docs that treat strong multi-user isolation as a broader trust-boundary decision; automation can identify defects but cannot choose the permanent product/security contract.

options.title: Require full isolation design first
options.body: Keep this PR blocked until it is rebased, fixes defaults/options/cache behavior, and provides two-user builtin/QMD proof against the canonical multi-user memory issue.

options.title: Narrow to explicit opt-in
options.body: Accept only a documented non-default experimental isolation mode with upgrade proof while leaving existing shared memory behavior unchanged by default.

options.title: Pause for canonical redesign
options.body: Pause or close this branch if maintainers want a fresh implementation under `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/63550` rather than rescuing this stale conflict-heavy branch.

recommendation.title: Require full isolation design first
recommendation.body: Keep this PR blocked until it is rebased, fixes defaults/options/cache behavior, and provides two-user builtin/QMD proof against the canonical multi-user memory issue.
